correctness.rationale: On the blowup of P2 at kappa infinitely near points of the infinity line, the canonical class and the strict transform have squares 9-kappa and 1-kappa. The quotient discrepancy gives Q=2/(kappa-1)(kappa H-sum E) for the regular case. For every other irreducible curve the line Bezout bound sum multiplicities<=degree proves positive intersection; only infinity and nonterminal exceptional curves can be null. In singular cases infinity supplies the exact kappa<=3 nef threshold. Q is nef big and orthogonal to infinity, so for kappa>=3 gives the Zariski decomposition. The all-maximal-block regular pencil contracts precisely the null configuration and has ample anticanonical class, giving the core model. Exact checker confirms 2014 finite configurations; infinite claim is proved geometrically.

value.rationale: The exact Fano/weak-Fano boundary and the canonical model are natural birational invariants of the Schubert surfaces. The result applies uniformly across unbounded maximal Jordan block lengths and arbitrary intermediate sizes and multiplicities, detects a genuine regular-versus-singular positivity transition at kappa=3, and identifies a canonical quotient that discards the finer block-size data while keeping eigenvalues and maximal lengths. The singular branch even remains big despite potentially negative anticanonical self-intersection, a structurally useful Zariski decomposition.
